cecservice: improve CEC compliance I have run cec-compliance tool from https://linuxtv.org/wiki/index.php/V4l-utils against cecservice. The tool complained about a couple of issues, this patch adds small tweaks to make cec-compliance tool more happy: 1. Set OSD name on the device (that does not seem to be required by the standard, but the tool complains if we don't have it set and it is an easy fix). 2. Instead of responding to standby request with 'feature abort' we simply ignore it (as per spec). Note - with that change the tool still complains that we haven't gone to standby while instructed to do so, but IMO that is OK as the specification allows for devices like for example PCs to ignore standby requests. With the patch applied the only error reported by the tool is about cecservice ignoring standby requests. BUG=chromium:828820 TEST=Run unit test and run cec-compliance tool. chrome-sdk: Add board and sdk version as gn args. This will let us propagate board/sdk values to test wrapper scripts generated at build time. In other words, we have gn rules that create a wrapper script around each test that's built. The gn rules bind whatever build-time-constants the tests need in the generated wrapper. (eg: output directory, path to test binary, runtime deps) For our cros use-case, that also includes the board/sdk-version. This explicitly lists those as gn args. (CL:1035602 declares them, so this should be safe to land after that.) Add programatic support for minijail '-G' flag to ProcessManager This CL is in preparation to run the shill process tree as a non-root user. Shill will soon spawn openvpn as user/group 'shill' before openvpn drops to user/group 'openvpn'. Startup process for openvpn needs write access to /dev/net/tun, which requires making shill user part of the 'tun' group and allowing the jailed openvpn process to inherit the supplementary groups from the 'shill' UID before dropping to 'openvpn'. Unfortunately, adding this single flag pushed the number of args in the ProcessManager:SpawnProcessInMinijailWithPipes function to 11, which is effectively prevented by gMock code, which only allows for mocking functions that use up to 10 arguments. Hence, this code also refactors the function to take in a struct with the 3 standard file descriptors instead of passing them each individually as arguments. BUG=chromium:649417 TEST=unittests pass, tested as part of larger sandbox shill debug CL Change-Id: I8254329cbe34de6551688b93d319f15489c3817b Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1050730 Commit-Ready: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> Tested-by: Micah Morton <mortonm@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Eric Caruso <ejcaruso@chromium.org>

arc: Kill ip_helper subprocess during setup when parent process exits In an arc-networkd crash (magic signature == [ASSERT] arc_networkd::IpHelper::InitialSetup), the daemon would crash with error message "SIOCGIFFLAGS failed". This happened when the ip_helper subprocess was started, but the parent process was killed (e.g. from user sign out) before the subprocess could finish setup. The child process would remain alive failing on an ioctl call until it finally timed out with "Container failed to come up". We prevent this by sending a NO-OP message over the control socket from the child to the parent process to make sure the connection is still alive. If it isn't, we can kill the child process. BUG=chromium:825365 TEST=Reproduced the bug several times on a Caroline by signing in to an account with ARC++ enabled, and immediately logging out. LOG(ERROR) before the Quit() statement was reached and the crash was gone. Notify ARC on boot that supervision state changed. Child accounts are able to graduate to regular accounts on Chrome, and ARC should disable CloudDPC and other supervision state when this happens. It will also be possible for some regular accounts to opt-in to supervision, in which case CloudDPC will need to be enabled. These bits are sent during boot instead of via a mojo IPC because it simplifies lifecycle considerations and avoids blocking on either side.
